scripts.hook: POV: Your Playwright tests are all failing... again 🔴 [bold red text slaps onto dark terminal screen at frame 1, 0-2s]
scripts.body: Scene 1 (2-8s): Extreme close-up of terminal — cascading red FAILED messages, error stack traces scrolling. Audio: frustrated exhale, muttered 'seriously?'. On-screen: 'not another flaky test…' | Pattern interrupt (8s): whip pan to developer hunched over keyboard, frantic typing. Scene 2 (8-16s): Jump cuts — checking selectors in DevTools, googling 'playwright test timeout', editing locators. On-screen: '47 minutes later...' in bold white text. | Pattern interrupt (16s): slow-motion zoom on finger hovering over Enter key. Dead silence. Scene 3 (16-25s): Finger presses Enter. Terminal loads... then GREEN checkmarks cascade down screen one by one. Audio: satisfying chime. On-screen: '💚 ALL TESTS PASSING' explodes onto screen in giant bold green text. | Scene 4 (25-30s): Developer leans back, exhales, small genuine smile. On-screen: 'Playwright hits different when it works.'
scripts.cta: Drop 🎉 if this is your entire QA life. Follow for Playwright tips that actually work.

Close-up on screen content, developer hands visible peripherally. Color narrative: angry red failing state transitions to euphoric green passing state. Loopable: final green screen can cut back to opening red for infinite rewatch loop.

scripts.hook: Your Playwright tests are flaky because of THIS one mistake [bold text slaps center screen, 0-1.5s]
scripts.body: Scene 1 (2-8s): Close-up of VS Code showing test with page.waitForTimeout(3000) — red highlight box draws around it. Audio: 'If your Playwright tests keep breaking in CI, I guarantee you are making this mistake.' On-screen: '❌ THE MISTAKE: hardcoded timeouts' | Pattern interrupt (8s): text pop-in with whoosh sound. Scene 2 (8-18s): Split-screen appears — bad practice left (red), correct pattern right (green). Audio: 'Playwright has built-in auto-waiting. Use waitForSelector or locator assertions — they retry automatically until your element is ready. Zero flakiness.' On-screen: '✅ THE FIX: waitForSelector + auto-waiting'. Code lines highlight and animate as spoken. | Pattern interrupt (18s): cut to terminal. Scene 3 (18-26s): Terminal shows green tests running 3x faster. Audio: 'Your tests just became ten times more stable. Same coverage, zero arbitrary waits.' On-screen: '10x more stable ⚡'. | Scene 4 (26-30s): On-screen: 'Save this 💾 — you will need it'

scripts.hook: Writing Playwright E2E tests with me ☕ — 3 patterns I always set up first [warm desk pan shot, 0-2s]
scripts.body: Scene 1 (2-12s): Camera pans across warm desk setup — coffee, laptop, Playwright docs visible on screen. Developer turns to face camera. Audio: 'Okay, new feature just shipped and I need E2E tests. Every time, I start with three things. First: test fixtures.' On-screen: '1️⃣ Test Fixtures First'. | Pattern interrupt (12s): jump cut to screen recording. Screen shows authSetup.ts fixture file being written. Audio: 'Fixtures let you share authenticated state across every test — you log in once, reuse everywhere. This alone cuts test run time in half.' On-screen: code showing storageState: authFile. | Pattern interrupt (20s): text pop-in '2️⃣'. Scene 2 (20-35s): Audio: 'Second — always Page Object Model. Separate your selectors from your logic. When UI changes, update one file and every test still passes.' On-screen: '2️⃣ Page Object Model'. Screen shows clean POM class structure. | Pattern interrupt (35s): camera cuts back to face-cam. Scene 3 (35-52s): Audio: 'Third, and this one is underrated — soft assertions. Use expect.soft() so your test reports ALL failures at once instead of stopping at the first one. Huge timesaver for complex user flows.' On-screen: '3️⃣ Soft Assertions: expect.soft()'. Screen shows side-by-side: normal assertion stopping at failure 1, soft assertion showing all 4 failures. | Scene 4 (52-60s): Pull back to show full workspace. Audio: 'These three setups save me hours every sprint. What is in your Playwright toolkit?' On-screen: 'What is your setup? 👇'
scripts.cta: What testing pattern do you always reach for first? Drop your must-have Playwright setup below 👇
onScreenText: Writing Playwright E2E tests with me ☕ (0-3s)
scripts.visualDirections: Vertical 9:16. Warm cozy home office with amber morning lighting. Mix of face-cam narration (medium close-up, shallow depth of field) and screen recording (VS Code code examples). Handheld feel with natural subtle movement during face-cam segments. Three clearly numbered sections each introduced with text pop-in. Companion energy — relaxed, conversational, authentic. Coffee mug present throughout for lifestyle warmth.

scripts.hook: I wasted 3 HOURS on manual testing... until I discovered Playwright [frustrated face, bold text, 0-2s]
scripts.body: Scene 1 (2-10s): Split screen — left side (desaturated, slow): developer manually clicking through web app, filling forms, repeating. Timer overlay counting up on left. Right side (bright, vibrant): placeholder showing what is coming. Audio: 'Before Playwright, every release meant three hours of manual regression testing. Click through every flow. Check every form. Pray nothing broke.' On-screen: 'Manual testing: 3 hrs per release ❌'. | Pattern interrupt (10s): hard cut, music beat drop. Scene 2 (10-20s): Full screen — Playwright terminal running 87 automated tests. Tests fly by at high speed. Timer on right counts down rapidly: 3:58, 3:30, 2:00, 0:04. Audio: 'Now I run 87 end-to-end Playwright tests covering the same flows. Four minutes. Every single time.' On-screen: 'Playwright: 87 tests in 4 minutes ✅'. | Pattern interrupt (20s): smooth zoom out to data visualization. Scene 3 (20-27s): Clean graphic: animated bar chart. Left bar (red, tall): Manual — 3 hours. Right bar (green, short): Playwright — 4 minutes. Text animates in: '23+ hours saved per month'. Audio: 'That is over twenty-three hours a month given back to actually building.' | Scene 4 (27-30s): Developer faces camera, relaxed. Audio: 'Share this with whoever on your team is still clicking through the app.' On-screen: 'Your team needs this 👇'
